battle.name: 鐵砂航線
battle.brief: 瑞典鐵礦經挪威水域南下。潛艇打的是噸位，護航打的是到港。卡面的雷諾FT不在這條航線上：1940年北挪威是滑雪山地部隊與商船的較量，法國在五月投降後那些坦克才落到德軍手中，成為次年東線裝甲部隊的一部分。

kit.name: 雷諾 FT
kit.history: 一戰量產輕戰車。可旋轉砲塔成為後來戰車的基本語法，而不是移動碉堡。

countries: 這場戰爭的名稱是一條航線，真正的交戰方卻有四方。核心是德國與英國。德國帝國海軍在海軍元帥雷德主持下以挪威海岸為戰區，由分遣支隊、Z型驅逐艦分隊與潛艇支隊執行對載礦商船的破壞；地面上的戰區指揮交給法爾肯霍斯特元帥的「威悉演習」作戰集群，目標是納爾維克的礦石裝載碼頭與通往瑞典的奧福特鐵路。德方的宣傳把此役說成是「保障」挪威中立與商運自由，實質卻是先行佔領這條原料供應線，並排除英國插手北歐的可能。英國方面由本國艦隊總司令海軍上將諾布爾統一指揮封鎖，北方巡邏隊沿挪威海岸攔截載礦商船，新編成的H艦隊以戰列巡洋艦Hood為旗艦北上，牽制德國的Scharnhorst與Gneisenau；海軍大臣邱吉爾力主在挪威領海大規模佈雷，把封鎖由「追船」改為「封海」。挪威在四月初仍是中立國，四月九日遭入侵後，國王哈康七世與政府拒絕吉斯林的投降主張，議會以壓倒多數票支持抵抗，國王與政府退往倫敦；挪威海軍、商船隊與破雷艦中隊整體倒向盟軍，成為北歐戰區英方最依賴的支援力量。瑞典自始保持中立，卻是這條航線的經濟當事人：私人擁有的基律納鐵礦公司與國營鐵路承擔全部開採與運輸，瑞典海軍還一度要求本國漁船避開戰區。這四方的關係可以概括為：德國要這條線，英國要切這條線，挪威被這條線拖入戰爭，瑞典靠這條線換取和平。
countriesEn: This war is named after a shipping route, but there were four parties to it, and at the core stood Germany and Britain. The German Reichsmarine, under the Grand Admiral, fought in Norwegian waters with detached squadrons, the Z-destroyer flotilla and the U-boat arm, striking at merchant ships loaded with ore; on land, the theatre command for Operation Weserübung was given to General der Infanterie von Falkenhorst, whose task was the ore-loading terminal at Narvik and the Ofotbanen railway running to Sweden. German propaganda described the campaign as the protection of Norwegian neutrality and free merchant shipping, but in substance it was a preemptive seizure of a raw-material supply line and an attempt to keep Britain out of northern Europe. On the British side the blockade was run by the Home Fleet under Admiral Sir Percy Noble; the Northern Patrol intercepted ore-laden ships along the Norwegian coast, and the newly formed Force H, with the battlecruiser Hood as flagship, moved north to contain the German Scharnhorst and Gneisenau. Churchill, as First Lord of the Admiralty, pressed for mass mining of Norwegian territorial waters, turning the blockade from chasing ships into closing the sea. Norway was still neutral at the beginning of April; after the invasion of 9 April the King Haakon VII and his government refused Quisling's demand for surrender, the Storting backed resistance by an overwhelming majority, and the King and government withdrew to London. The Norwegian navy, merchant marine and minesweeper flotillas went over to the Allied side and became the most trusted support of the British forces in the northern theatre. Sweden remained neutral throughout, yet was the economic party to the route: the privately owned Kiruna mining company and the state railways carried the whole of extraction and transport, and the Swedish navy at one point required its own fishing vessels to keep clear of the war zone. The arrangement can be summed up this way: Germany wanted the line, Britain wanted it cut, Norway was dragged into the war by the line, and Sweden traded the line for peace.
people: 德國方面，希特勒在戰前的公開講話中把「取得瑞典的鐵」列為對英戰爭的目標之一，四月九日批准了「威悉演習」；元帥尼古勞斯·馮·法爾肯霍斯特以英國參謀部自身的戰間期經驗為藍本擬出方案，指揮三個山地師與若干步兵師的北挪威分遣支隊；海軍元帥埃里希·雷德把戰列巡洋艦Scharnhorst、Gneisenau與重巡洋艦Admiral Hipper調入挪威海域，Scharnhorst由赫爾穆特·海耶率領，Gneisenau由京特·呂特延斯率領，而率驅逐艦支隊破壞商船與佈雷的是埃里希·貝。第3山地師師長福伊爾施泰因率部攻佔納爾維克，並於四月二十八日在城郊陣亡。德軍還保留了一支由艦隊司令直接指揮、專門打擊礦運的力量，這本身就說明這條線在德方帳目中的份量。英國方面，海軍上將珀西·諾布爾統轄本國艦隊，海軍參謀長達德利·龐德策劃雷區，海軍大臣邱吉爾把切斷北歐原料列為頭號任務，H艦隊指揮官詹姆斯·薩默維爾在海峽中與德國主力艦周旋；潛艇HMS Triton的艇長在四月十二日把裝載礦石的Rauenfels送入海底。挪威一端，國王哈康七世拒絕退位也拒絕投降，總司令奧托·魯格指揮北挪威的挪威部隊與英軍守備部隊在納爾維克一帶抵抗德軍山地師；四月下旬挪威第六師團與英軍一度反攻收復納爾維克，德軍第三山地師再取回該城，雙方在峽灣與山口的雪地裡反覆拉鋸。
peopleEn: On the German side, Hitler had already named getting Sweden's iron among the war aims he aired in public speeches before 1940 and approved Operation Weserübung on 9 April. General der Infanterie Nikolaus von Falkenhorst drew up the plan from the British staff's own interwar experience and commanded three mountain divisions and several infantry divisions sent north. Grand Admiral Erich Raeder moved the battlecruisers Scharnhorst and Gneisenau and the heavy cruiser Admiral Hipper into Norwegian waters, with Hellmuth Heye in Scharnhorst, Günther Lütjens in Gneisenau, and Erich Bey leading the destroyer force that mined the channels and struck at the ore shipping. The 3rd Mountain Division under General Feurstein took Narvik, and its commander was killed in action outside the town on 28 April. Germany also kept a force under the direct command of the naval commander reserved for attacking the ore traffic, which says a great deal about how the line was valued on the German accounts. For Britain, Admiral Sir Percy Noble commanded the Home Fleet, the Chief of the Naval Staff Dudley Pound planned the minefields, Churchill made the severing of northern raw material his first priority, and Force H under Admiral James Somerville contained the German capital ships in the narrows; the captain of HMS Triton put the ore-laden Rauenfels on the seabed on 12 April. On the Norwegian side King Haakon VII refused both abdication and surrender, and General Otto Ruge commanded the Norwegian troops and the British garrison around Narvik against the German mountain troops; a Norwegian and British counter-attack in late April briefly retook the town before the 3rd Mountain Division recovered it, the two sides grappling back and forth across snow-filled fjords and passes.
kits: 卡面這件雷諾FT是法國1917年定型的兩噸級輕戰車，全車重約兩噸，乘員兩人，裝甲約六十三毫米，車體前部裝三十七毫米砲，尾部配一挺機槍，旋轉砲塔把機動性與正面防護結合成一體，確立了此後戰車的基本語法；1917至1918年間法國生產約三萬五千輛，另有數千輛輸出與改裝，是第一次世界大戰中產量最大的坦克。但1940年四月的北挪威戰線上沒有這種兵器：德軍投入的是山地步兵師與步兵師，英軍與挪威軍是徒步與滑雪的山地部隊，決定勝負的裝備是機場跑道、七十五毫米山砲、迫擊砲、機槍與可以在短跑道起降的攻擊機，整場戰爭裡戰車一次也沒有出現。真正上陣的裝備是另一套清單：水雷、潛艇、護航驅逐艦與巡洋艦、封鎖巡邏機、破雷艦、商船、礦石裝載碼頭與裝載滑槽、奧福特鐵路的蒸汽機車與列車，以及船上的高射砲與武裝登船隊。德國佈在維恩格利亞海峽的水雷一次報廢兩艘裝礦商船，英國潛艇HMS Triton在航道口擊沉的Rauenfels亦然；這些裝備在卡面那輛坦克出現的年代早已成熟，只是在另一個戰場上發揮作用。卡面兵器的真正去向也在同一年間：法國五月投降，數千輛雷諾FT成為德軍繳獲物，1941年德軍第四裝甲師曾以改裝的FT-17編成臨時戰鬥群投入東線——那些戰車的鋼鐵，最終仍是靠卡面這條航線輸送的礦石煉出來的。
kitsEn: The Renault FT on the card is the French two-tonne light tank typed in 1917. It weighed some two tonnes, carried a crew of two, had roughly 63 mm of armour, mounted a 37 mm gun at the front of the hull and a machine gun at the rear, and its rotating turret joined mobility to frontal protection in a way that became the basic grammar of the tank for everything that came after. Between 1917 and 1918 France built about 35,000 of them, with several thousand more converted, which made it the most numerous tank of the First World War. No vehicle of that kind stood on the northern Norwegian front in April 1940. Germany committed mountain and infantry divisions; the British and Norwegian forces were foot and ski infantry; the decisive equipment was airfield, 75 mm mountain guns, mortars, machine guns and attack aircraft able to take off and land on short strips. Not one tank appeared in this war. The equipment that actually fought belonged to a different inventory: mines, submarines, escort destroyers and cruisers, blockade patrol aircraft, minesweepers, merchant ships, the ore pier and its loading chutes, the locomotives and trains of the Ofotbanen, together with the ships' own anti-aircraft guns and armed boarding parties. The German minefield off Vingleia wrote off two ore-laden merchantmen in a single strike, and so did the British submarine HMS Triton at the mouth of the fjord. All of it was mature technology by the time the tank on the card appeared; it was simply being used on a different battlefield. The card weapon has a destination of its own in the same year: after France surrendered in May, several thousand Renault FTs became German captures, and in 1941 the 4th Panzer Division formed a temporary battle group around converted FT-17s for the eastern front. The steel in those tanks had ultimately been smelted from the very ore this route carried.
tactics: 這場戰爭的戰術可以用四個字概括：封、登、撤、追。德國的順序是先封後登。四月八日，Z型驅逐艦分隊與魚雷艇在維恩格利亞海峽外佈雷，同時以艦炮攻擊正等在海峽裡等領港的兩艘裝礦商船，一沉一傷，並在掩護救援時擊沉英國護航驅逐艦HMS Afridi；一天之後「威悉演習」同時在五個方向登陸，最北一路直取納爾維克，工兵在峽灣內架設浮橋與駁船，把火砲與車輛送上岸，山地師則以滑雪板和雪橇翻越峽灣南側的山口直插城內，掩護與補給全靠浮橋與空投維持。英國的戰術不是登陸對抗，而是封鎖加撤退：一面以北方巡邏隊在挪威海岸追截載礦商船，一面由潛艇在峽灣口伏擊，1940年10月起改為在挪威領海大量布雷，把封鎖從追船升級為封海，1941年11月更在納爾維克外海佈下水雷陣。撤退的技術是這一戰最冷的一頁：英軍與挪威軍在四月上旬把納爾維克的守備部隊與滯留商船一批批撤走，商船必須在峽灣內等待引航員登船，那幾個小時的等待正是最脆弱的窗口，也是德軍第一次佈雷得以奏效的場所。商隊的掩護方式分層展開：巡洋艦在外、驅逐艦在內、破雷艦掃雷、潛艇伏擊，配合海空偵察與封鎖巡邏，提醒護航的存在本身就是威懾。至於這條戰爭的補給線本身：礦石自基律納經約一百四十公里的鐵路到納爾維克，冬季波羅的海沿岸結冰，航線才轉到挪威無冰的外海，春季航季一開，整個德國的煉鋼爐都壓在這條水道上。
tacticsEn: The tactics of this campaign can be summed up in four words: close, land, withdraw, hunt. The German order was to close first and land second. On 8 April the Z-destroyer flotilla and the torpedo boats laid mines off the Vingleia strait and opened fire with their guns on two ore-laden merchantmen waiting inside the narrows for a Norwegian pilot, sinking one and damaging the other, and while covering the rescue they sank the British escort destroyer HMS Afridi. A day later Operation Weserübung landed simultaneously in five directions, the northernmost thrust aimed straight at Narvik; engineers bridged the fjord with pontoons and barges to bring guns and vehicles ashore, mountain troops pushed into the town on skis and sledges over the passes to the south of the fjord, and the lifeline was held by those bridges and by air supply. The British answer was not a landing battle but blockade plus withdrawal: the Northern Patrol hunted ore ships along the Norwegian coast, submarines ambushed ships at the fjord mouths, and from October 1940 the Admiralty switched to large-scale mining of Norwegian waters, raising the blockade from chasing ships to closing the sea, with a minefield laid off Narvik in November 1941. The technique of withdrawal is the coldest page of this war. The British and Norwegian forces pulled the Narvik garrison and the merchant ships held in the fjord out in batches through the first days of April, and a ship had to wait inside the fjord for a pilot to come aboard; those hours of waiting were the most vulnerable window of all, and they were the reason the first German minefield worked at all. Convoy cover was layered: cruisers outside, destroyers inside, minesweepers clearing a channel, submarines waiting to ambush, with air reconnaissance and blockade patrol to remind everyone that escort was present. As for the supply line itself, ore came some 140 km by rail from Kiruna to Narvik; in winter the Baltic coast froze and the traffic had to move down the ice-free Norwegian seaboard, so the moment the spring sailing season opened, every steel furnace in Germany was riding on that one waterway.
data: 這條航線的數字本身就是戰略。1930年代後期，德國每年自瑞典進口鐵礦約一千萬噸，統計口徑雖有出入，但都指向同一量級，其中經納爾維克出海的部分約六百多萬噸，構成德國鐵礦進口的最大一宗；瑞典礦石含鐵量約六成上下、磷偏高，正好配合德國既有的轉爐設備。鐵路方面，奧福特鐵路自納爾維克至國境約一百零六公里，全線至基律納約一百四十公里，列車滿載約一千噸；納爾維克的礦石裝載碼頭年裝載能力約六百多萬噸，是當時世界上最大的散貨碼頭之一。戰役數字集中在四天：四月八日，總噸位約三萬四千噸的兩艘裝礦商船觸雷沉沒，英國護航驅逐艦HMS Afridi（排水量約一千三百五十噸）同日被擊沉；四月九日至十日，英軍自納爾維克撤出守備部隊與滯留商船；四月十二日，潛艇HMS Triton擊沉八千六百噸的Rauenfels，船上約三千噸鐵礦隨之沉入海底。陸戰方面，德軍為攻取納爾維克投入的山地師約六千人，挪威第六師團與英軍守備部隊不足三千人。距離上，自基律納礦區到魯爾區的工廠，鐵路加海運近三千公里。佔領之後，德國每年仍有數百萬噸鐵礦經此線運回國內，直到1944年底航線才被戰爭本身拖垮。
dataEn: The figures on this route are the strategy. In the late 1930s Germany imported on the order of ten million tonnes of Swedish iron ore a year; the statistical definitions vary, but they all point to the same order of magnitude, and something over six million tonnes of the total left by sea from Narvik, making Swedish ore the single largest source of German ore imports. Swedish ore ran about sixty per cent iron with high phosphorus, which fitted the converter plant Germany already had. On the railway side the Ofotbanen ran some 106 km from Narvik to the border and about 140 km on to Kiruna, with trains carrying roughly a thousand tonnes; Narvik's ore pier could handle over six million tonnes a year and was among the largest bulk terminals in the world. The fighting figures cluster into four days. On 8 April two ore-laden merchantmen of about 34,000 tons gross in total struck mines and sank, and the British escort destroyer HMS Afridi, of about 1,350 tons displacement, was sunk the same day; between 9 and 10 April the British evacuated the Narvik garrison and the merchant ships held there; on 12 April the submarine HMS Triton sank the 8,600-ton Rauenfels, taking some 3,000 tonnes of ore down with her. On land, the German mountain force committed to taking Narvik numbered about 6,000 men against fewer than 3,000 Norwegians and British in and around the town. In distance, the run from the Kiruna mining district to the Ruhr works was close to 3,000 km by rail and sea together. After the occupation Germany still shipped several million tonnes of ore a year down this line, and it was the war itself, not any decision on the ground, that finally choked it in late 1944.
cause: 打起嚟的原因有三層。最外層是德國的原料焦慮：德國的鋼鐵長期依賴北歐礦產，瑞典的基律納與馬爾姆貝里特是全球最大、最純的磁鐵礦來源之一，納粹在重整軍備的第一年裡就把「把瑞典的鐵弄到手」寫進公開談話，理由是沒有這些礦，德國的軍工產能撐不過1939年以後的消耗。當時的官方說法是「維護挪威的中立與商運自由」，真正的軍事計劃卻是把航線連同港口、鐵路、礦山一次拿下，同時排除英國在北歐插手的可能。第二層是英國的封鎖邏輯：第一次世界大戰末期英國已經用「切斷原料」作為對德戰爭的骨幹，1939年冬海軍部就研究在挪威海岸佈雷，邱吉爾接手海軍部後把這件事推上前台，英國的算盤是礦石不進德國，德國的炮就少一門。第三層是直接導火線：1940年2月，德國戰鬥巡洋艦Altmark在挪威水域被迫交還被其扣押的英國船員，挪威政府就英國拆船廠事件向英方交涉，德國以此為由向挪威提出一系列要求，包括在奧福特鐵路與納爾維克碼頭取得通行權乃至軍事過境權，挪威全部拒絕。同時，冬季波羅的海沿岸結冰，礦石只能改走挪威無冰的外海，春季航季一開，這條最脆弱的血管正好暴露在海峽雷區與潛艇的獵場之中，於是外交、封鎖與航海季節三股力量在四月疊到了一起。
causeEn: There are three layers to the reason this war was fought. The outermost was German anxiety about raw materials. German steelmaking had long depended on northern ores, and the Kiruna and Malmberget deposits in Sweden were among the largest and richest sources of magnetite in the world; in the first year of the rearmament the Nazis put getting Sweden's iron into public speeches, on the argument that without it German war industry could not survive the consumption of the years after 1939. The official line was that they were defending Norwegian neutrality and freedom of merchant shipping, while the real military plan was to take the route with its port, its railway and its mines in one stroke and to forestall any British presence in northern Europe. The second layer was the British logic of blockade. Severing raw material had been the backbone of the British war against Germany in the closing phase of the First World War, the Admiralty had studied mining Norwegian waters in the winter of 1939, and Churchill, taking over the Admiralty, drove the business to the front of the board on the calculation that no ore meant one fewer German gun. The third layer is the immediate spark. In February 1940 the German battlecruiser Altmark was forced in Norwegian waters to give back the British seamen it had been holding; the Norwegian government pressed the British over the seizure of shipping in British yards, and Germany used the episode to put a series of demands to Norway, including rights of passage and military transit over the Ofotbanen railway and the Narvik terminal. Norway refused all of it. At the same time the Baltic coast froze in winter and the ore had to move down the ice-free Norwegian seaboard, so with the opening of the spring sailing season the most fragile blood vessel in Europe lay exposed in a mined strait and in the hunting ground of the submarines, and diplomacy, blockade and the sailing calendar all came together in April.
impact: 這場戰爭的影響沒有落在會戰上，而是落在結構上。對德國而言，佔領挪威在短期內保住了礦運，但1940年6月法國投降帶來了洛林的鐵礦與摩澤爾的礦石，德軍的原料缺口被這一大片新礦區填補，再加上1941年8月從蘇聯取得的糧食與石油，瑞典礦石從「生死線」降格為「方便的通道」，這才是英國長年封鎖最終沒有能壓垮德國工業的根本原因：原料缺口在別處被補回來了。對英國而言，封鎖的形式與效果都有限：英國水面艦隊在北挪威的追逐，等於給了德國以巡洋艦逐漸奪取挪威海岸制海權的時間；1940年7月英方宣佈關閉北歐中立國水域的商運後，德國改用挪威旗與中立國船隻沿整條挪威海岸做「沿岸航運」，把大船的運輸拆成小船的接力；真正令這條線縮水的不是艦艇而是水雷，1940年10月「威爾弗雷德行動」與1941年11月「甘特利特行動」在挪威領海與納爾維克外海佈下的水雷，才是讓航運量在兩年內大幅下降的主力。對挪威而言，國家被佔領五年，挪威商船隊因租賃英美船舶而損失慘重，卻也成為盟軍跨大西洋運力的骨幹。對瑞典而言，局面更難：在被佔領的鄰國面前維持中立，只能一邊大量供貨，一邊聽任盟國在北極水域布雷；1944年10月美軍轟炸瑞典馬爾姆斯拉特一帶的鐵路設施，機體墜毀引發爆炸，事故之後瑞典與盟國之間生出裂痕。長期看，這段歷史成了「補給線決定戰爭」最常被引用的案例之一：德國花了六個師的代價守住一條通往瑞典的線，而線的另一端是他自己的工廠。
impactEn: The effects of this war were structural rather than decisional. For Germany, taking Norway kept the ore moving in the short term, but France's surrender in June 1940 brought the ore of Lorraine and of the Moselle, and the German raw-material gap was filled by that new mining area; with Soviet grain and oil from August 1941 on top of it, Swedish ore was demoted from a life-line to a convenient channel, and that is the real reason a blockade sustained for years never crushed German industry. The raw material was made good somewhere else. For Britain the blockade was limited in both form and effect. The chase by British surface ships in the far north gave Germany the time to take the Norwegian coast off the sea with its cruisers, and after the closure of neutral north European waters to commerce in July 1940 Germany shifted to running coastal traffic under Norwegian and neutral flags along the whole Norwegian coast, breaking the movement of large ships into relays of small ones. What really shrank the flow was not warships but mines: the minefields laid in Norwegian waters under Operation Wilfred in October 1940 and off Narvik under Operation Gauntlet in November 1941 were what cut the tonnage sharply over two years. For Norway the country was occupied for five years, and the Norwegian merchant marine, which lost heavily while serving Allied charters, became the backbone of Allied Atlantic lift. For Sweden the position was harder still: neutrality in front of an occupied neighbour meant shipping ore in volume while accepting that the Allies would mine the Arctic waters, and the US bombing of the railway works around Malmslätt in Sweden in October 1944, with a bomber crashing into the embankment and detonating, left a rift between Sweden and the Western Allies. In the long run this episode became one of the most cited cases of the supply line deciding the war: Germany spent the equivalent of six divisions to hold a road running to Sweden, and the far end of that road was its own factories.
result: 打到最後是這樣收場的：1940年4月的北挪威戰役，德國以海軍切斷峽灣、陸軍同時登陸的方式拿到納爾維克與奧福特鐵路，礦石在短暫停頓之後恢復下海；英國在挪威北部的努力則以撤退與戰術勝利交錯著收場——HMS Afridi沉沒是四月的損失，潛艇HMS Triton擊沉Rauenfels是英方在北挪威為數不多的直接戰果，而英軍放棄在挪威登陸、把守備部隊與滯留商船撤走，則是一場沒有決戰的撤退。往後的勝負是英國的雷區與德國的運量之間的較量：1940年7月關閉北歐中立國水域的商運，1941年底在納爾維克外海佈雷，德國被迫把大船改為小船沿岸接力，礦運量在兩三年間明顯縮水，卻靠瑞典的鐵路與挪威的船隊硬撐到戰爭末期；1944年底，德軍改為主要走陸路，把礦石從瑞典直接用列車運過國境，這條線於是從「海上的航線」變回「陸上的鐵路」，直到1945年挪威與德國先後投降，航線才回到和平狀態。收官時的最後一段是戰後的算盤：瑞典在歐洲重建時成為西歐最重要的鐵礦供應者之一，納爾維克與奧福特鐵路的產能重新被西方使用；而這場戰爭留下的最大教訓，是它沒有一場會戰，卻把一個工業大帝國的血管掐在手裡——掐住的人用的是水雷、潛艇和耐心，被掐的人用的是巡洋艦和登陸艦。
resultEn: It ended like this. In the northern Norwegian campaign of April 1940 Germany took Narvik and the Ofotbanen by sealing the fjords with the navy while landing with the army, and the ore traffic resumed after a short interruption. The British effort in northern Norway ended in a mixture of withdrawal and tactical success: the loss of HMS Afridi was April's price, the submarine HMS Triton sinking the Rauenfels was one of the few direct British results in the area, and the abandonment of the projected landing in Norway and the evacuation of the garrison and the merchant ships held there was a retreat without a decisive battle. What followed was a contest between British minefields and German tonnage: the closing of north European neutral waters to commerce in July 1940, the minefield off Narvik at the end of 1941, the forcing of large ships into relays of small coastal craft, and a visible shrinkage of the tonnage over two or three years, held up by Swedish rail and Norwegian ships until the end of the war. In late 1944 Germany switched mainly to land transport, moving ore from Sweden across the border by train, and the route turned from a sea lane back into a railway; it did not return to peacetime until Norway and Germany had both surrendered in 1945. The last accounting is a postwar one: in the rebuilding of Europe Sweden became one of the most important suppliers of iron ore to the West, and the capacity of Narvik and the Ofotbanen was put back to work. The largest lesson the war left is that it contained no battle at all, and yet it put an industrial empire's blood vessel in a man's fist: the hand that gripped used mines, submarines and patience, and the hand that was gripped used cruisers and landing craft.
